concepts.title: Fractional Units
concepts.definition: Cut one whole into some equal pieces; every single piece is one fractional unit (a unit fraction like 1/4).
concepts.key_idea: A fraction with 1 as the numerator representing one part of a whole divided into n equal parts.
question_patterns: what is the fractional unit if a unit is divided into 5 parts
express one part of a whole divided into 10 equal shares
find the unit fraction for a division into 8 parts
calculate the share of one person when one roti is shared among 9 children
What is the fractional unit when a whole is cut into 6 parts?
Name the unit fraction of a division into 12 equal shares.

solution_steps.action: identify the number of equal parts
solution_steps.explain: The denominator n represents the total number of equal parts the whole is divided into.
A unit fraction always has 1 as the numerator.

solution_steps.action: write the unit fraction as 1 over n
solution_steps.explain: The result names one equal piece of the whole, so the share is 1/n.

concepts.title: Fractions as Equal Shares
concepts.definition: Share a number of things equally among a number of people, and fractions say how big one share is (3 rotis among 4 gives 3/4 each).
concepts.key_idea: Top count = things shared; bottom count = people sharing.
question_patterns: how much does each child get if 3 rotis are shared among 4 children
find the share when 5 glasses of juice are shared by 6 friends
calculate the weight of each guava if 3 guavas weigh 1 kg
what is the fraction of a cake each person gets if 2 cakes are shared by 5 people
Share 5 rotis among 8 children -- how much each?
How big is one share when 4 cakes feed 6 friends?

solution_steps.explain: The number of items is the numerator and the number of people is the denominator.

solution_steps.action: write the fraction with items on top
solution_steps.explain: The numerator counts the things being shared out.

solution_steps.action: write the fraction with people on the bottom
solution_steps.explain: The denominator counts the equal shares, giving the final fraction items/people.

concepts.title: Numerator and Denominator
concepts.definition: In a written fraction the top figure is the numerator; the bottom figure, the denominator.
concepts.key_idea: The lower count names the unit; the upper count says how many of those units you hold.
question_patterns: identify the numerator and denominator in 5/6
what is the top number of a fraction called
in the fraction 3/4, what does 4 represent
name the parts of the fraction 7/10
In 9/13, which number is the denominator?
How many units does the numerator 7 stand for in sevenths?

solution_steps.explain: The number above the line is the numerator.
The number below the line is the denominator.
The denominator names the unit (how many equal parts make one whole) and the numerator counts how many of those units are taken.

concepts.title: Mixed Fractions Definition
concepts.definition: A quantity bigger than one whole can be written as a whole part next to a part smaller than one -- that pair is a mixed fraction (2 2/3).
concepts.key_idea: Values above one whole get a whole part plus a part under one.
question_patterns: identify the whole part and fractional part in 2 2/3
Is 5 1/8 bigger than one whole -- why?
Point out the whole part and the part under one in 3 5/6.

solution_steps.explain: The integer part of the mixed number.
The proper fraction part following the whole number.

solution_steps.action: confirm the value exceeds one whole
solution_steps.explain: Since the whole part is at least 1 and the fractional part is non-negative, the mixed fraction represents a quantity greater than or equal to one whole.

concepts.title: Converting Improper Fraction to Mixed Fraction
concepts.definition: When the top count beats the bottom count, the value tops one whole and a mixed form is available.
concepts.formula: whole = numerator // denominator; remainder = numerator % denominator
concepts.key_idea: Divide the numerator by the denominator to find the whole number and the remainder.
question_patterns: how many whole units are there in 7/2
Convert 31/7 to whole units plus a fraction.

solution_steps.explain: The quotient is the whole number part.
The remainder becomes the numerator of the fractional part.
Combine the whole number and the remainder over the denominator to form the mixed fraction.

concepts.title: Converting Mixed Fraction to Improper Fraction
concepts.definition: Rewrite each whole as a full set of the fractional pieces, then count all pieces together.
concepts.key_idea: Multiply the whole number by the denominator and add the numerator.

solution_steps.explain: This converts the whole units into fractional parts.
Add the existing fractional parts to the converted whole parts.
The denominator remains the same.

concepts.title: Equivalent Fractions
concepts.definition: Two fractions that measure the same amount though written with different units are equivalent (1/2 and 3/6).
concepts.key_idea: Scale both counts by one non-zero factor and the value never changes.
question_patterns: calculate an equivalent fraction for 3/4 with denominator 40

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the top by the chosen factor.
Multiply the bottom by the same factor.
The new fraction new_num/new_den has the same value as the original because both counts were scaled equally.

concepts.title: Simplest Form (Lowest Terms)
concepts.definition: A fraction sits in lowest terms when nothing bigger than 1 divides both of its counts.
concepts.key_idea: Divide both counts by their biggest shared factor to arrive there.

solution_steps.explain: Divide the numerator by a shared factor.
Divide the denominator by the same shared factor.
The fraction s_num/s_den is in lowest terms when no factor greater than 1 divides both counts.

concepts.title: Comparing Fractions
concepts.definition: To see which of two fractions wins, rewrite them as same-unit fractions and compare the counts.
concepts.formula: v1 = num1 * den2; v2 = num2 * den1
concepts.key_idea: One shared unit turns the comparison into a straight count-off.
question_patterns: Arrange 3/4, 5/6 and 7/8 from smallest to largest.

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the denominators of both fractions.
Multiply first numerator by second denominator.
Multiply second numerator by first denominator.
The fraction with the larger scaled numerator is greater.

concepts.title: Addition of Fractions (Brahmagupta's Method)
concepts.definition: Put both fractions into one shared unit, then simply add the counts.
concepts.key_idea: Common fractional units allow direct addition of numerators.
question_patterns: what is the total volume if 2/3 L and 3/4 L are mixed

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the denominators to get a common fractional unit.
Scale the first numerator.
Scale the second numerator.
Add the scaled numerators together.
The sum is the new numerator over the common denominator.

concepts.title: Subtraction of Fractions
concepts.definition: Put both fractions into one shared unit, then take one count away from the other.
concepts.key_idea: Match the units first; afterwards only the counts get subtracted.
question_patterns: how much distance is left if 1/2 km is covered out of 7/10 km

solution_steps.explain: Multiply the denominators.
Scale the first numerator.
Scale the second numerator.
Subtract the second scaled numerator from the first.
The difference is the result numerator over the common denominator.
